domestic_evidence: No GST turnover band, GeM/CPPP tender award or annual-report domestic/export split could be retrieved. DuckDuckGo search backend returned connection errors on all attempts ("searx: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>"), so no domestic-supply record was located. Note: the customs data itself shows the Indian-side port lanes (Kilaraipur ICD, Panitankinaxalbari) which are consistent with goods moving from a Punjab factory to the Nepal border, but this is export traffic, not domestic-market supply.
note: Export side is factually confirmed, not merely declared: dated customs records with HS 87120010, destination Nepal, and BOL 9737842, plus a 1854-record history and named foreign buyers in Jordan, DR Congo, Netherlands and Mexico. Declared HS 871200 matches the actual recorded code 87120010 — no HS correction needed. The trading name 'Leader Cycles' is the bicycle brand appearing in the goods description ('LEADER BICYCLE 40CM...'), while the exporter of record is JINDAL FINE INDUSTRIES; the legal entity therefore appears to be the manufacturer/exporter behind the brand, role best described as manufacturer (not a pure trader). Domestic Indian-market supply is unverified — no GST band or public-procurement record obtained because the search tool was unavailable, so domestic_status is 'unknown', not 'none_found'. Revenue and export volume figures are not public on the free pages: null, not estimated. Caveat on completeness: only 5 of the 1854 claimed shipment rows were visible without a subscription; the aggregate counts and counterparty names are as displayed by the source and were not independently cross-checked against a second database (volza, eximpedia, trademo and importgenius all returned 403 / JavaScript challenge).
